spec.title: codkit PROP-003: Configuration, data conventions, the owners map, common format rules

status.comment: standalone settings, patch-set config, installed safety policy and artifact formats

format-rules.title: 1. Common rules of every codkit format

facts.SCHEMA-VERSION-FIELD: Every format carries its schema version - an integer in the field named after the format itself (for example, `"codkitConfig": 1`, `"codkitOverlay": 2`).
facts.SCHEMA-MIGRATION-RULE: The migration rule after the first user: a reader accepts version `N`; on `N+1` and above it fails with code 2 and the text «the format is newer than the tool, update codkit»; a version below the current one it reads by the rules of that version and writes the current one at the next write. The one-off pre-user exception of the owner, 2026-08-31: the D5 metadata formats `patch/overlay/resource/rule/own/inventory` moved from v1 to v2 through a hard rename of the former field into `cause`; there were no external users and no meaningful values of the former field, so v2 deliberately refuses v1 and no legacy reader is shipped.
facts.FILE-BYTE-RULES: All format files: UTF-8 encoding without a BOM, LF line endings, a trailing LF is mandatory.
facts.JSON-DETERMINISTIC-SERIALIZATION: JSON is serialized deterministically: an indent of two spaces; object keys in the order defined by the schema (NOT alphabetically); arrays in the order defined by the schema (usually sorted by `id` or by path).
facts.SCHEMAS-ARE-ZOD: The format schemas are described by Zod schemas as the single source of the static type and of runtime validation (`common/PROP-000` `##CODKIT-VALIDATOR-ZOD`); the diagnostic text of a schema error is formed in the terms of the code registry of PROP-012 §2, not as the raw output of the validator.

p.SETTINGS-FILE: `~/.codkit/settings.json` selects the external roots independently: the strict schema `{"codkitSettings":1,"patchesDir":"/absolute/path","forkDir":"/absolute/path"}`. Both path fields are optional and absolute only; an unknown field, a wrong type or another schema version gives `CK-E-CONFIG`.

facts.PATCHES-DIR-PRECEDENCE: patchesDir: `--patches-dir` → `CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR` → the settings `patchesDir`; the absence of all three is a diagnosed refusal for the commands that need a patch set.
facts.FORK-DIR-PRECEDENCE: forkDir: `--fork-dir` → `CODKIT_FORK_DIR` → the settings `forkDir`; the absence of all three is allowed only for the commands that do not need the tree.
facts.PATH-BASE-RULE: A relative CLI or env path is resolved against the cwd of the process. The settings accept absolute paths only. `codkit.json`, a neighbouring directory and the location of toolRoot are never a fallback source of a root.
facts.DISJOINT-ROOT-GUARD: After canonicalization toolRoot, patchesDir and forkDir must be pairwise disjoint, nesting included. A violation stops the command before the patch set is read and before any mutation.

tr.td: the name of the upstream tag, e.g. `"1.135.0"`
40 hex, the full SHA of the tag commit
`YYYY-MM-DD`, the date of the pin commit
40 hex; the root commit of the upstream history (see `##ANCHOR-COMMIT-RULE`)

**removed in schema 2.** The own root is `typeConfig.ownRoot`, a full path from the tree root (`##CFG-TYPE-AND-TYPECONFIG`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`); the anchor stays for the citations that name the field this replaced
the identifier of the project type, e.g. `"vscode"`; one safe identifier, resolved through the registry (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-REGISTRY`)
the section the type validates with its own schema; its first field is `ownRoot`, a path from the tree root that the engine reads by itself, e.g. `"src/vs/patchset"`
the URL of the fork on the hosting (for `publish`)
an explicit patch-set-relative path to the build-watch data of a particular fork
an explicit patch-set-relative path to an additive-only extension of the conventions

safe paths from the tree root, a file or a directory, that `publish --scrub` leaves out of the release (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#PUBLISH-EXCLUDE`); `publish` has no other field, it is written last, and only when present

p.ANCHOR-COMMIT-RULE: `upstreamAnchorCommit` is the SHA by whose reachability the tree is recognized as «the microsoft/vscode history» (the origin is checked by the reachability of a known commit, not by the name of a remote). The value is computed once when the configuration is created: `git rev-list --max-parents=0 <pin.sha>` (the root commit of the history; if there are several roots, the lexicographically smallest SHA is taken). It is committed in `codkit.json` and does not change when the pin is raised.

p.CFG-TYPE-AND-TYPECONFIG: **Schema 2 (PROP-016).** `codkit.json` carries `"codkitConfig": 2`, the required `"type": "<identifier>"` and the required `"typeConfig": { ... }`, whose first field is `ownRoot` - a full path from the tree root. The engine validates the universal fields of the table above and hands `typeConfig` to the type, which validates it with its own schema and refuses with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the field (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CONFIG-FIELD`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`). One patch set, one type. The row `ownDirName` of the table above is the schema-1 field it replaces.

p.CFG-SCHEMA-1-IS-REFUSED: **There is no compatibility layer.** A `codkit.json` without `type` is schema 1 and is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` that names the two fields to add - `type` and `typeConfig.ownRoot` - and nothing else; no command reads schema 1 and no code path infers a type from `ownDirName` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SCHEMA-2-REQUIRED`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#DECISION-NO-COMPATIBILITY-LAYER`). The single existing consumer is migrated inside the campaign, with its own gates as the proof.

p.LOCAL-CONFIG-RULE: `codkit.local.json` contains only optional non-pin operational overrides (`typeConfig`, the branch/ref prefixes, `publishRemoteUrl`, `publish.exclude`; in schema 1 the first of them was `ownDirName`). `publish.exclude` is the one list that is joined with the base instead of replacing it: a local file can leave more out of a release, never less. The `type` itself is not overridable locally: one patch set declares one type and it is a shared invariant of the repository. It does not accept `pin`, `upstreamAnchorCommit`, the schema field, the location roots or references to a safety/build policy. The root paths belong to the CLI, the environment and the user settings alone.

p.PIN-CHANGES-ONLY-BY-CYCLE: After the initial bootstrap of a patch set the pin changes only by the canonical commit of an upgrade cycle.

p.config-valid-sample: A valid sample (the `upstreamAnchorCommit` value is a placeholder of the example; in a real file it is the computed SHA):

p.CONFIG-INVALID-SAMPLE: An invalid sample and the expected diagnostics: a file with `"pin": {"tag": "1.135.0"}` (no `sha`) → exit 2, the message `CK-E-CONFIG: codkit.json: pin.sha is required (full 40-hex commit sha of the pin tag)`.

p.CONVENTIONS-SINGLE-DEFINITION: The mandatory base policy lives only in `toolRoot/config/conventions.json`; the CLI, the checks, the CI and the agent protocols read it. A file with the same path under patchesDir never shadows the installed policy.

tr.td: the subsystems allowed in intervention ids; the values are the project type's defaults (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-009#VSCODE-CONVENTIONS-DEFAULTS`): `["workbench","editor","platform","extensions","build","product","base","server","test"]`
the regular expression of an intervention id: `"^CK-(workbench|editor|platform|extensions|build|product|base|server|test)-[0-9]{3}$"`

the marker forms by file extension (PROP-004 §1); the shape of the value is fixed by the M0 implementation: the key is an extension with the dot, the value is `{"open":"<the prefix before codkit:>","close":"<the tail or an empty string>"}`; keys that start with `_` are documentation and do not take part in matching

the globs of the files for which patches are forbidden; the values are the project type's (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-002#VSCODE-FORBIDDEN-PATCH-TARGETS`): `[".config/1espt/**"]` (a file with mixed line endings) plus the overlay targets (the `**/*.json` exceptions - PROP-005 §5)
the ids of the services that must not be overridden (the bootstrap services; the list is the project type's - VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-009#FORBIDDEN-SERVICES-SEED`)
the cleanup whitelist of the fresh mode (PROP-011 §4); the values are the project type's (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-002#VSCODE-CLEANUP-WHITELIST`)

p.FORBIDDEN-SERVICES-SEED: Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-009#FORBIDDEN-SERVICES-SEED; the address stays for citations.

p.CONVENTIONS-EXTENSION: If `conventionsExtensionFile` is given, the path must stay inside patchesDir after symlinks are resolved. The strict schema `codkitConventionsExtension:1` may add `subsystems` (the effective idPattern is derived from the union), additional `forbiddenPatchTargets`, `forbiddenServiceIds` and `markerComment` for new file extensions only. It cannot delete, replace or weaken the base prohibitions, change the layer order, an existing marker form, the intervention types/categories or the cleanup policy.

p.NO-HIDDEN-POLICY-OVERRIDE: A patch-set file `codkit/config/conventions.json` without an explicit `conventionsExtensionFile` is ignored. Even with an explicit reference the content is treated as an additive extension, not as a replacement of the shipped policy.

p.BUILD-WATCH-SELECTION: By default the build wrapper reads `toolRoot/config/build-watch.json`. Only an explicit `buildWatchFile` selects the strict versioned profile of a particular fork; the patch set is the project policy chosen by the user, but a hidden copy under the same name is not taken into account. The path must be relative and contained inside patchesDir. Every channel must have at least one `errorLine` or `errorCountLine`; unknown fields are forbidden. The author of a custom profile keeps green/red log fixtures and confirms that an error does not become exit 0.

facts.OWNER-MUST-EXIST: The `owner` value of any artifact must be a key of `owners`; otherwise `verify` gives exit 1, `CK-E-OWNER-UNKNOWN`.
facts.CODEOWNERS-GENERATED-LATER: The CODEOWNERS file of the hosting is generated from this map (the command is not in the MVP; the map itself is already in the MVP: the inventory needs the «subsystem → owner» routing).

p.ARTIFACT-METADATA-DICTIONARY: Every layer gives the inventory the same set of fields: `id`, `layer`, `type`, `category`, `owner`, `reason`, `link`, `cause`, `pin`, `contract-tests`, plus the computed `subsystem` (from the id) and `files` (the targets of the intervention). The carrier for a patch is the `.ckpatch` header (PROP-004 §3); for an overlay/resource/rule it is the fields of their JSON (PROP-005); for own and entry-module it is the records in `delta/own/patchset.delta.json` (PROP-005 §3).
